subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 19-year-old woman with severe nodulocystic acne that has failed topical retinoids and oral antibiotics is prescribed oral isotretinoin. Her physician documents a negative pregnancy test and requires two forms of contraception before the first dose and throughout therapy. The patient asks what would happen if she became pregnant while taking the medication.
question: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of fetal exposure to this drug?

options.text: Neural tube defects with elevated amniotic fluid alpha-fetoprotein
Ebstein anomaly with an atrialized right ventricle

explanation_correct: Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) is a vitamin A derivative that is highly teratogenic because it interferes with homeobox gene expression during craniofacial and cardiac development. The classic malformations are cleft palate and cardiac abnormalities, which is why a negative pregnancy test and two forms of contraception are mandatory before and during therapy.

explanation_incorrect.A: Neural tube defects such as spina bifida and anencephaly follow first-trimester folate antagonism (eg, methotrexate) or valproate exposure rather than retinoid exposure.
explanation_incorrect.B: Chondrodysplasia punctata with nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses is the warfarin embryopathy and reflects inhibited vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ebstein anomaly with an atrialized right ventricle is classically associated with first-trimester lithium exposure.
explanation_incorrect.D: Limb-reduction defects with facial hypoplasia are the thalidomide embryopathy, not the retinoid embryopathy.

educationalObjective: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen that disrupts homeobox gene expression and causes cleft palate and cardiac malformations, so pregnancy must be excluded and prevented during therapy.
